title: Esoteric Comment Cryptography (Beethoven Constants)
pattern: Adding obscure, highly personal, or historic comments to justify magic numbers instead of creating a descriptively named domain constant.
why_bad: The comment acts as an enigma. It requires deep trivia knowledge (e.g., that Beethoven died in 1827, which is 0x723 in hexadecimal) while failing to explain *why* the value `0x723` is functionally necessary for the compiler or execution environment.
detection: Magic numbers or hexadecimal literals annotated with non-technical, cryptic comments that do not reference specifications, RFCs, or hardware datasheets.
counterexample: Comments citing specific section numbers of official technical specifications, RFCS, or hardware registers (e.g., `// RFC 7230 Section 3.2`).
fix:
Replace the magic number with an intent-revealing constant name and remove the self-indulgent comment.
```rust
const BEETHOVEN_DEATH_YEAR_HEX: u32 = 0x723;
```
